security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode code that reads the (pre-fix) ACLIC spec and implements software interrupt priority comparison replicates the operator precedence bug: writing expressions like `prio & MASK >= threshold` which evaluates as `prio & (MASK >= threshold)` instead of `prio >= (threshold & MASK)`. This would occur in any OpenSBI handler that does software-based priority filtering, or when OpenSBI configures interrupt priority thresholds via AIA CSRs and later validates priority values in software.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: bitwise AND operator (`&`) combined with comparison operator (`>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`) on the same line without explicit parentheses around the mask operation — specifically patterns like `expr & MASK >= threshold` or `expr & MASK <= threshold`
security_spec.summary: Spec typo fix: operator precedence bug where `iprio[i] & MASK >= threshold` was missing parentheses around `threshold & MASK`. OpenSBI could replicate this in software priority logic (e.g., HSM interrupt save/restore or AIA CSR manipulation), causing incorrect interrupt preemption decisions that block higher-priority interrupts.

findings.finding: No instances of the operator precedence vulnerability pattern (bitwise AND `&` combined with comparison operator `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` without explicit parentheses) were found anywhere in the OpenSBI codebase. The codebase consistently uses safe patterns: either fully parenthesized `(expr & MASK)` before comparison, or logical AND (`&&`) between separately grouped expressions. There is no SMNIP-related code in the current master branch. The PLIC priority save/restore helpers (commits 34da6638ad7b, 8509e46ca63a) use array indexing, not bitwise-and-priority-threshold comparisons.
findings.snippet: N/A - vulnerability pattern not present in codebase
